After the rollback, the service reports healthy with an error rate of about 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying, and look into why it was promoted despite failing in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened incident INC-0001 (SEV2), which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks with about an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it in us-east, us-west and eu-west. A human approver signed off. Afterwards the service reports healthy, with the error rate down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 says what failed, what I rolled back and the follow-up work. My first attempt to create it timed out. I checked that nothing had been created, then retried with the same idempotency key so only one incident could exist and on-call would only be paged once.

The pre-release build of v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging but still went to production. The incident lists two next steps: find the root cause before redeploying v2.3.1, and look into why it was promoted despite failing in staging.
